clue.text: Plain Sailing (it's a surprise old recording about Disney stowing family away on ship)

indicators.note: on means placed after, the ship coming last
about means the exclamation goes round the Disney piece

parts.note: AH is the exclamation of someone taken by surprise

indicators.note: stowing ... away means the Disney name holds the family word inside it
part of the phrase stowing away, packing something inside out of sight

parts.note: Walt Disney, the film-maker
kin are your relatives
EP, an extended-play record, an old format
Noah's ark was a ship

explanation.surface: A newspaper review of some show called Plain Sailing, a surprise discovery involving an old record and Walt Disney's relatives stowing away aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: something described with this phrase is very easy, just as plain sailing means a smooth, trouble-free task.

clue.text: 12 guides …

definitions.meaning: 12 refers to the 12 down light, the simple matters at the end of the 10 across phrase, as in easy as ABC
primers or basic guides, like the old ABC railway guides

explanation.surface: Twelve guides lead into the next clue's chemistry.
explanation.walkthrough: '12' stands for the 12 down words: something as easy as ABC. The ABC was also a classic British railway timetable guide.
explanation.definitionFit: The rudiments of a subject are its alphabet, and simple primers that teach basics carry that title.

clue.text: See 11
… simplest compound of its kind is a piece of cake to 18

indicators.note: a piece of means only a run of letters taken from inside the following words

parts.note: with 18 replaced by the 18 across answer, the words read cake to Nestor, which holds the answer

explanation.surface: Following on from 1 down, the simplest compound of its kind is said to be child's play for a wise old man.
explanation.walkthrough: Replace 18 with NESTOR, and the answer sits inside 'cake to NESTOR'. 'simplest' and 'of its kind' only dress the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A ketone is an organic chemical with a carbonyl group bonded to two carbon atoms, acetone being the best known.

clue.text: So as to preserve name, fashion store cuts blab about film

indicators.note: cuts means slices into, so the store and so as pieces go inside
about means the blab phrase is turned round

parts.note: to let on is to blab a secret

indicators.note: to preserve means to keep something inside

parts.note: C&A, a clothing chain once common on British high streets, spelt C AND A

explanation.surface: A fashion shop trims gossip about a movie while protecting someone's identity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the blab phrase round, 'to preserve' holds the name letter, and 'cuts' sends the rest into the middle. C&A is a British high-street clothing chain, written out as C AND A.
explanation.definitionFit: Notes on a Scandal is a 2006 film starring Judi Dench and Cate Blanchett.

clue.text: Sucker 15 putting last of shoes over last of four feet

indicators.note: putting one letter over another means substituting it in that place

parts.note: a vacuum cleaner kept in the house is this famous brand of sucker

indicators.note: the final letter of the four word
the final letter of the shoes word

explanation.surface: A shoe-fitter's note about four feet, with something sucking.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 15 as its answer: a sucker at home is a HOOVER, the vacuum-cleaner brand. Swap its last letter, R (end of four), for S (end of shoes).
explanation.definitionFit: Hooves are the horny feet of horses and similar animals.

clue.text: See 1 across
Rising through time, The Old Man of Hoy's inwardly flickering glimmer?

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the whole is read from the bottom up
through means going inside the period word

parts.note: an era is a period of time

indicators.note: inwardly means the jumbled letters are held inside

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father, the old man

indicators.note: flickering means unsteady, so the letters move about

parts.note: the words of Hoy, the possessive s giving no letter

explanation.surface: A beam rises through time from the famous sea stack, the Old Man of Hoy, as a glimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' reverses the whole build, as suits a down entry. The Old Man of Hoy is a famous sea stack in Orkney, but here the Old Man is father.
explanation.definitionFit: Metaphor: a faint sign of hope is like a glimmer of light, a small promising sign.

clue.text: Don't tell anyone I'm slightly alarmed about papers agent finally secreted in 6

indicators.note: about means the exclamation is turned backwards

parts.note: eek is the squeak of mild alarm

indicators.note: in means the papers piece goes inside the 6 across word

parts.note: 6 refers to the 6 across light, the last word of the 1 across phrase

indicators.note: secreted means hidden away inside

parts.note: ID, identification papers

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of agent

explanation.surface: A secret agent, slightly alarmed, whispers about hiding papers in a public space.
explanation.walkthrough: The 6 across word is the last word of the 1 across phrase; the papers, with the agent's last letter secreted in them, go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: keeping something secret, hiding it from others, is a request to say nothing.

clue.text: Duck Soup badly wanting US director to probe hoax insider appointment

indicators.note: to probe means to go inside, so these pieces sit within the hoax word

parts.note: a con is a hoax or swindle
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

indicators.note: badly signals the letters of soup are jumbled
wanting means lacking, so the letters of US are taken from the mix

parts.note: Jacques Tati, the French film director; the US beside it belongs to the deletion

explanation.surface: A review panning the Marx Brothers film Duck Soup, minus its American director, with a hoax insider landing a job.
explanation.walkthrough: Duck Soup and US director are false pairings: the film title splits, and the director beside US is Jacques Tati, a Frenchman.
explanation.definitionFit: Co-opting is when a body's existing members elect a newcomer themselves, an appointment made from inside.

clue.text: Let oneself go and freely gratify one's kleptomaniac urges?

definitions.meaning: a thief's literal reading: help oneself to items without effort

explanation.surface: Advice to relax, followed by a jokey suggestion of shoplifting without restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the phrase literally: a kleptomaniac lifts objects, and doing it freely means helping oneself without fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for relaxing and not overexerting oneself; literally, helping oneself to possessions as a thief would.

clue.text: Befogged, exhausted and ultimately flagging, refuse what's effortless

indicators.note: and joins the inner pieces that go together inside the fog word; the real container signal is the be- of befogged, meaning surrounded by

parts.note: befogged means lost in fog, so it supplies the weather word fog, which wraps round the pieces that follow
all in means worn out

indicators.note: ultimately picks the last letter

parts.note: offal is waste or refuse

explanation.surface: A walker lost in fog, exhausted and flagging, refuses something that looks easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Befogged' does double duty: it supplies the fog and says the rest is wrapped in it. 'refuse' looks like a verb but is the noun, waste.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: something as easy as tumbling from a fallen tree trunk is a proverbially simple task.

clue.text: See 10
Newest lassie on manoeuvres — no sweat — makes territorial detachment?

indicators.note: manoeuvres move troops around, so the letters are rearranged
no here means without, so the letters of the sweat word are taken from the mix

explanation.surface: A young woman newly on army manoeuvres finds it no sweat, while someone carves off a piece of territory.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the twelve letters of NEWEST LASSIE, with S, W, E, A and T removed, rearrange into the seven-letter answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To enisle is to make into an island or isolate, detaching a piece of land from its surroundings.

clue.text: Cooking only this sovereign food is money for old rope

indicators.note: cooking means the letters are worked up into something new

explanation.surface: Preparing only royal food is easy money.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: ONLY, the answer and FOOD together mix into MONEY FOR OLD ROPE, so take the letters of ONLY and FOOD from that phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor is a supreme ruler of an empire, a monarch.

clue.text: Start to Sing Something Simple: soldier describes that as wise, ironically

indicators.note: start to means the first letter
describes means draws round, so the soldier word encloses the other

parts.note: a soldier ant is a worker ant
pie, as in easy as pie

explanation.surface: Starting a radio show of simple songs, a soldier mockingly calls it clever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something Simple' is PIE, from 'easy as pie'. Sapient is often used mockingly, hence 'ironically'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapient means wise or discerning, and is now chiefly used with mocking intent.

clue.text: Headers from Ronaldo and Neymar missing — anyhow, more than comfortable

indicators.note: anyhow means in any old way, so the letters are rearranged
missing means the picked letters are absent from the mix
headers are the first letters of the footballers' names

explanation.surface: Football talk: no headers from Ronaldo and Neymar, but the team still feels more than comfortable.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of MORE THAN, less R and N (the initials of Ronaldo and Neymar), rearrange to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being relaxed and at ease somewhere, as if in one's own house, is a common idiomatic sense.

clue.text: Elementary group VII choice after a bit of scientific enlightenment

indicators.note: after means the earlier piece comes first in the answer
a bit of means just the first letter of the next word

parts.note: astatine (At) and iodine (I) are elements in group VII, the halogens
or offers a choice between alternatives
iodine, symbol I, is another group VII element

explanation.surface: A chemistry teacher offers a choice of halogen element, leading to a flash of scientific insight.
explanation.walkthrough: The periodic table's group VII includes astatine and iodine, so 'group VII choice' reads as AT OR I.
explanation.definitionFit: Satori is the Zen Buddhist term for sudden spiritual awakening or insight.

clue.text: Last up to welcome learner is husband, well impressed

indicators.note: to welcome means to take in, so these letters go inside

parts.note: whoever is last up has stayed longest abed, in bed the longest
L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A late riser lets in a learner, and the husband is quite taken with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last up' is the person who has lain LONGEST ABED; L, IS and H go between its B and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Something firmly fixed by long tradition is deeply stamped in, a figurative sense of being well impressed.

clue.text: 'Not rocket science, Einstein's principles,' gathered wise old man

indicators.note: gathered means collected together in a new arrangement
principles here means the first, principal letters of each word

explanation.surface: Someone quotes Einstein's principles as being no rocket science, and a sage collects them.
explanation.walkthrough: Mix NOT with R, S and E, the initial letters of rocket, science and Einstein's.
explanation.definitionFit: Nestor is the aged, wise counsellor of the Greeks in Homer, and his name means any sage elder.

clue.text: What's stopping unthinking makeover

indicators.note: is stopping means plugging the middle of the next word

parts.note: rash means hasty and thoughtless
eh is the exclamation for what?

explanation.surface: Something halts a thoughtless redesign.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehash reworks old material into a supposedly new form, a superficial makeover.

clue.text: Pushover that was Her Majesty's undercover marksman

parts.note: snip is an old word for a cinch or certainty, something easy
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Something that was a pushover for a royal undercover sharpshooter.
explanation.definitionFit: A sniper fires from a hidden position, a marksman under cover.

clue.text: Range of tobacco found in doss? Nuff said

indicators.note: found in means the answer sits within the next words

explanation.surface: Tobacco left in a dosshouse; enough said.
explanation.definitionFit: Snuffs are powdered tobacco preparations for sniffing, sold in a range of kinds.

clue.text: Who's gonna have trouble selling new coat?

definitions.text: Who's gonna have trouble selling new coat?

parts.words: Who's gonna have trouble selling new coat?
parts.note: split 3,4 the answer reads as slang saying a salesman is not, the one who'll struggle; whole, it means a fresh layer of paint

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper wonders which salesperson will struggle to shift a new coat.
explanation.walkthrough: Split into REP AIN'T, the answer reads as a cheeky reply: the sales rep isn't gonna. As a whole word it means a fresh coat of paint, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Applying a fresh layer of paint gives a surface a new coat.

clue.text: Satisfactory? Nothing to talk about

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the chat word runs backwards

parts.note: yak is informal for chatter

explanation.surface: Is it fine? Nothing worth discussing.
explanation.definitionFit: Okay is the informal word for acceptable or all right.

clue.text: 2-rolling frame that could be open for a gimme?

definitions.text: frame that could be open for a gimme?

indicators.note: rolling means turning over, so the letters change places

parts.note: 2 refers to the 2 down light, the last two words of the 11 down phrase

explanation.surface: A rolling log by a frame that could be open for an easy chance.
explanation.walkthrough: An open goal is an unguarded net, the easiest of scoring chances.
explanation.definitionFit: A goal is the framed net in football, and an open one is an easy score, a gimme.

clue.text: See 25
It's not hard to 10 for many, a BBC day off

indicators.note: off means out of order or wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Many viewers are said to find something easy on a BBC holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 10 as the 10 across phrase's first word: the definition becomes an easy thing to steal. The fourteen letters of FOR MANY A BBC DAY rearrange to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: stealing from an infant is proverbially effortless, so anything very easy is likened to it.

clue.text: Woman in the north always fills iron

indicators.note: fills means goes inside the iron symbol

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
ay is a dialect word for always, used in Scotland and northern England

explanation.surface: A northern woman is forever ironing.
explanation.definitionFit: Faye is a woman's first name, so it serves as an example of a woman.

clue.text: A breeze ruffling lily-pads on eastern side of loch

indicators.note: on means following, the mixed letters coming after
the eastern side of a word written across is its right-hand half
ruffling disturbs, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A breeze ruffles lily pads on the east side of a Scottish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eastern side of' takes CH, the right half of loch; then ILDSPLAY, the anagram of LILYPADS from 'ruffling'. 'A breeze' looks part of the scene but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: something infants could manage is simple, and a breeze is slang for an easy task.
